newsitem.title: PERU: Peru police evict six journalists at siege site.
newsitem.headline: Peru police evict six journalists at siege site.

text.p: Peruvian police removed six journalists on Saturday from the roof of a building near the besieged residence of the Japanese ambassador in Lima, where Marxist rebels are holding 73 hostages.

Five photographers and a television cameraman, mostly from international news agencies, were ordered down from the vantage point they had manned in shifts, hauling up food by rope, for the 32 days since the siege began.
The order was signed by police Gen. Fernando Gamero Febres and obliged the journalists to come down "for strict reasons of security".

"I do not agree with this; I would have liked to stay till the end," said Johnnie Laurente, a photographer for the local La Republica newspaper and one of the two local journalists removed. The eviction took place without incident.
A larger group of local reporters was removed from the same roof on Thursday.
Hundreds more journalists are camped out in the environs of the besieged residence, behind police cordons placed at a distance of two city blocks on all four sides.
The Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels stormed the residence Dec. 17, taking more than 500 hostages to demand the release of some 400 imprisoned MRTA members.

Among the 73 captives they are still holding are the Japanese and Bolivian ambassadors to Peru, about two dozen Japanese businessmen and diplomats, Peru's Foreign Minister Francisco Tudela and other government and security officials, and a brother of Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori.
